sections.title: KidHabit Hero User Guide
sections.html:
This guide describes all KidHabit Hero features as users see and use them, then shows which features connect to one another. Each file begins with “In this guide” and ends with “Related,” so you can move from one feature to the features that go with it without starting your search again.

KidHabit Hero helps parents and children build good habits through small daily actions: parents assign tasks, children mark them complete, parents approve them, and children collect stars to redeem rewards chosen by their parents. The app does not use stars to compare children or judge their character (see the principles).

sections.title: Contents
sections.html:
Contents

  1. Getting started: ways to enter the app, sign in, set up a family, roles, language, and the demo.
  2. Child screen: tasks, completion, postponing, timers, stars, levels, streaks, badges, rewards, rankings, mascots, morning letters, journals, and dream city.
  3. Today and approvals: tasks awaiting approval, rewards awaiting approval, each child’s progress, weekly review, statistics, printing, and sharing.
  4. Designing habits: task management, the library, the 47-habit framework, programmes and cues, age-based roadmaps, and the reward library.
  5. Family and settings: child profiles, device pairing, caregivers, account, PIN, appearance, privacy, reminders, app installation, data, and taking a break.
  6. Habit science: principles, the four phases, suggestion logic, 16 character profiles, and 7 ways of giving.
  7. Plans and payment: trials, plans, PayOS, activation, coupons, refunds, and email.
  8. Refer a friend: referral codes, 10% discounts, 30% commissions, and withdrawals.
  9. Security and privacy: PINs, pairing codes, consent, children’s data, and data deletion.
  10. Connection map and scenarios: dependency diagrams, end-to-end journeys, and troubleshooting.
  11. Glossary.

sections.title: Conventions in this guide
sections.html:
Conventions in this guide

  • In-app paths use the form Area → Item, for example Family → Settings.
  • “A plan” means the family is in a trial period or has a plan that has not expired (7).
  • “PIN if one has been set” means the action runs only after this browser has entered the correct, valid parent PIN (5).
  • Prices, thresholds, and time limits are the values at the time of writing; the authoritative source is in the technical documentation linked at the end of each file.
